attractions.name: Kwame Nkrumah Mausoleum
attractions.aliases: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park; Nkrumah Mausoleum; Kwame Nkrumah Mausoleum and Memorial Park
attractions.description: Memorial and final resting place of Ghana's first president, Kwame Nkrumah, located in downtown Accra. It features a marble mausoleum, a museum and landscaped grounds.

attractions.name: W. E. B. Du Bois Memorial Centre for Pan African Culture
attractions.aliases: Du Bois Centre; W.E.B. Du Bois Centre; Du Bois Memorial Centre
attractions.description: Research centre, museum and mausoleum in Accra dedicated to the Pan-Africanist W. E. B. Du Bois, who spent his final years in Ghana.

attractions.name: Labadi Beach
attractions.aliases: La Pleasure Beach; Labadi Pleasure Beach
attractions.description: Accra's best-known public beach, located at La in the city's east and popular for its weekend entertainment.

attractions.name: Fort James
attractions.aliases: James Fort; Fort James, Accra
attractions.description: A British fort built in 1673 on the Accra coast, used historically in the transatlantic slave trade.

attractions.name: Osu Castle
attractions.aliases: Christiansborg Castle; Fort Christiansborg
attractions.description: A castle at Osu in Accra, built by the Danish in the 17th century and long used as Ghana's seat of government.

attractions.name: Efua Sutherland Children's Park
attractions.aliases: Children's Park Accra; Efua Sutherland Park
attractions.description: A public children's park in central Accra named after the playwright Efua Sutherland.

attractions.name: Accra Mall
attractions.aliases: Accra Mall, Spintex; Accra Shopping Mall
attractions.description: A large shopping mall in Accra, opened in 2008 on the Spintex Road.

attractions.name: Tema Harbour
attractions.aliases: Port of Tema; Tema Port
attractions.description: Ghana's principal seaport, located at Tema east of Accra.

attractions.name: Achimota Forest
attractions.aliases: Achimota Forest Reserve
attractions.description: A forest reserve in the Achimota area of Accra, an important urban green space.

attractions.name: Lake Bosumtwi
attractions.aliases: Lake Bosomtwe; Bosumtwi Crater Lake
attractions.description: A meteorite crater lake in the Ashanti Region, the only natural lake in Ghana.

attractions.name: Armed Forces Museum
attractions.aliases: Ghana Armed Forces Museum; Kumasi Military Museum
attractions.description: A military museum in Kumasi housed in a former British fort, tracing Ghana's military history.

attractions.name: Centre for National Culture
attractions.aliases: Kumasi Cultural Centre; National Cultural Centre, Kumasi
attractions.description: A cultural centre in Kumasi with craft shops, a museum and performance spaces.

attractions.name: Bonwire
attractions.aliases: Bonwire Kente Village; Kente weaving village
attractions.description: A town in the Ashanti Region renowned as the home of Asante kente cloth weaving.

attractions.name: Ntonso
attractions.aliases: Ntonso Adinkra Village; Adinkra cloth village
attractions.description: A town near Kumasi known for traditional adinkra cloth printing.

attractions.name: Bobiri Butterfly Sanctuary
attractions.aliases: Bobiri Forest and Butterfly Sanctuary; Bobiri Butterfly Sanctuary
attractions.description: A forest reserve and butterfly sanctuary near Kumasi with hundreds of butterfly species.

attractions.name: Rattray Park
attractions.aliases: Rattray Park, Kumasi
attractions.description: A modern recreational park in Kumasi with gardens, fountains and a children's play area.

attractions.name: Asante Traditional Buildings
attractions.aliases: Asante Traditional Buildings UNESCO Site; Asante Shrines
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site of surviving traditional Asante shrine buildings in the Ashanti Region.

attractions.name: Manhyia Palace
attractions.aliases: Manhyia Palace, Kumasi
attractions.description: The official residence of the Asantehene in Kumasi and a centre of Asante traditional authority.

attractions.name: Kumasi Fort
attractions.aliases: Kumasi Fort and Military Museum
attractions.description: A 19th-century fort in Kumasi that now houses the Ghana Armed Forces Museum.

attractions.name: Ahwiaa
attractions.aliases: Ahwiaa Wood Carving Village
attractions.description: A town near Kumasi known for traditional wood carving.

attractions.name: Besease
attractions.aliases: Besease Traditional Shrine; Besease Asante building
attractions.description: A village in the Ashanti Region with a traditional Asante shrine building that forms part of the UNESCO Asante Traditional Buildings.

attractions.name: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology
attractions.aliases: KNUST; Kumasi University of Science and Technology
attractions.description: Ghana's leading science and technology university, whose park-like campus at Kumasi is a notable landmark.

attractions.name: Elmina Castle
attractions.aliases: Sao Jorge da Mina; St. George's Castle; Elmina Castle
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site built by the Portuguese in 1482, the oldest European building in sub-Saharan Africa.

attractions.name: Kakum Canopy Walkway
attractions.aliases: Kakum Canopy Walk; Kakum Walkway
attractions.description: A suspended canopy walkway through the rainforest of Kakum National Park.

attractions.name: Fort Coenraadsburg
attractions.aliases: Fort St. Jago; Fort Coenraadsburg
attractions.description: A hilltop fort at Elmina built by the Dutch in the 17th century.

attractions.name: Fort Lijdzaamheid
attractions.aliases: Fort Patience; Fort Lijdzaamheid
attractions.description: A Dutch fort built at Apam in 1697, also known as Fort Patience.

attractions.name: Fort Goede Hoop
attractions.aliases: Fort Good Hope; Fort Goede Hoop
attractions.description: A Dutch fort built in 1705 at Senya Beraku in the Central Region.

attractions.name: Fort Komenda
attractions.aliases: Fort Komenda, British Komenda
attractions.description: A fort at Komenda in the Central Region.

attractions.name: Assin Manso Slave River Site
attractions.aliases: Assin Manso Slave River; Donkor Nsuo
attractions.description: A heritage site at Assin Manso on the slave route where captives were bathed before being sold.

attractions.name: Cape Coast Castle Museum
attractions.aliases: Cape Coast Castle Museum, Ghana
attractions.description: A museum inside Cape Coast Castle illustrating the history of the transatlantic slave trade.

attractions.name: Elmina Java Museum
attractions.aliases: Java Museum, Elmina
attractions.description: A museum at Elmina documenting the history of African soldiers recruited by the Dutch in the 19th century.

attractions.name: Gramophone Records Museum and Research Centre of Ghana
attractions.aliases: Gramophone Records Museum; Cape Coast Gramophone Museum
attractions.description: A museum in Cape Coast preserving historic gramophone records and Ghanaian highlife music.

attractions.name: Fort William Lighthouse
attractions.aliases: Cape Coast Castle Light; Fort William Lighthouse
attractions.description: A lighthouse associated with Fort William at Cape Coast.

attractions.name: Cape Coast Sports Stadium
attractions.aliases: Cape Coast Stadium; Robert Mensah Stadium
attractions.description: A multi-purpose stadium in Cape Coast used for football and athletics.

attractions.name: Biriwa Beach
attractions.aliases: Biriwa; Biriwa Beach, Central Region
attractions.description: A coastal town and beach in the Central Region of Ghana.

attractions.name: Akaa Falls
attractions.aliases: Akaa Waterfalls; Akaa Falls, Kade
attractions.description: A waterfall near Akaa in the Eastern Region, close to the Atewa Range.

attractions.name: Asenema Waterfall
attractions.aliases: Asenema Falls
attractions.description: A waterfall near Asenema in the Eastern Region, popular for hiking.

attractions.name: Obosomase Waterfalls
attractions.aliases: Obosomase Falls
attractions.description: Waterfalls at Obosomase in the Akuapem area of the Eastern Region.

attractions.name: Atewa Range Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Atewa Forest; Atewa Range
attractions.description: A forest reserve in the Atewa Range noted for its high biodiversity and bauxite deposits.

attractions.name: Adomi Bridge
attractions.aliases: Adome Bridge; Volta Bridge
attractions.description: A suspension bridge over the Volta River at Atimpoku, opened in 1957.

attractions.name: Kwahu Plateau
attractions.aliases: Kwahu Ridge; Kwahu Mountains
attractions.description: A highland plateau in the Kwahu area of the Eastern Region, known for its escarpment views and paragliding.

attractions.name: Bunso Eco Park
attractions.aliases: Bunso Arboretum; Bunso Eco Park
attractions.description: A conservation and recreation park at Bunso in the Eastern Region, formerly the Bunso Arboretum.

attractions.name: Fuller Waterfalls
attractions.aliases: Fuller Falls
attractions.description: A waterfall in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

attractions.name: Kpong Dam
attractions.aliases: Kpong Hydroelectric Dam
attractions.description: A hydroelectric dam on the Volta River at Kpong in the Eastern Region.

attractions.name: Akuapem Hills
attractions.aliases: Akuapem Ridge; Akuapem Mountains
attractions.description: A range of hills in the Eastern Region hosting towns such as Akropong, Aburi and Mampong.

attractions.name: Akwawa Mountain Peak
attractions.aliases: Akwawa Mountain; Akwawa Peak
attractions.description: A mountain peak near Nkawkaw in the Eastern Region listed among the region's tourist sites.

attractions.name: The Big Tree at Oda
attractions.aliases: Big Tree, Oda; Oda Big Tree
attractions.description: A giant historic tree at Akim Oda listed among the Eastern Region's tourist sites.

attractions.name: Nzulezo Stilt Village
attractions.aliases: Nzulezu; Nzulezu Stilt Settlement; Nzulezo Village
attractions.description: Nzulezo is a village built entirely on stilts and platforms over Lake Tadane near Beyin in the Jomoro District, and was added to the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List in 2000. Reached only by canoe, it is one of the few ancient stilt settlements left in the world.

attractions.name: Fort Saint Anthony
attractions.aliases: Forte de Santo Antonio; Fort Santo Antonio; Fort Sint Anthony
attractions.description: Fort Saint Anthony was built by the Portuguese in 1515 near Axim and was later captured and expanded by the Dutch before passing to the British in 1872. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979 and is now owned by the Ghanaian state.

attractions.name: Fort Sebastian
attractions.aliases: Fort San Sebastian; Sao Sebastiao de Shema; Shama Fort
attractions.description: Fort San Sebastian is a former Portuguese fort at Shama, originally built in the 1520s and later held by the Dutch, that forms part of the UNESCO-listed Forts and Castles of Ghana. It is one of the oldest European trading forts on the Gold Coast.

attractions.name: Butre Beach
attractions.aliases: Butre Bay; Boutry Beach; Butre Coastal Bay
attractions.description: Butre Beach lies in the sheltered bay below Fort Batenstein in the Ahanta West District, framed by the historic village of Butre. The bay was historically used as a safe anchorage and landing point by European traders.

attractions.name: Akwidaa Beach
attractions.aliases: Akwidaa Fishing Village; Akwidaa Coastal Village
attractions.description: Akwidaa is a coastal fishing village in the Ahanta West District between Cape Three Points and Princes Town. Its beach and the nearby Fort Dorothea ruins are visited for their scenery and colonial history.

attractions.name: Dixcove Beach
attractions.aliases: Infuma Beach; Dixcove Coastal Beach
attractions.description: Dixcove Beach is a fishing-community beach in the Ahanta West District below the promontory of Fort Metal Cross. It is a working landing site for fishermen and a base for visitors to the fort.

attractions.name: Western Regional Museum
attractions.aliases: Sekondi Museum; Western Region Museum
attractions.description: The Western Regional Museum in Sekondi is administered by the Ghana Museums and Monuments Board and displays artefacts relating to the history and cultures of the Western Region. It is housed in a colonial-era building in the regional capital area.

attractions.name: Gold Fields Ghana Tarkwa Mine
attractions.aliases: Tarkwa Gold Mine; Goldfields Tarkwa; Tarkwa Nsuaem Gold Mine
attractions.description: The Gold Fields Ghana Tarkwa Mine is a large open-pit gold mining operation at Tarkwa in the Tarkwa-Nsuaem Municipality. Tarkwa is home to the University of Mines and Technology and is one of Ghana's principal gold-mining centres.

attractions.name: Ghana Goldfields Mine at Tarkwa
attractions.aliases: Tarkwa Goldfields; Ghana Goldfields
attractions.description: The popular Ghana Gold Fields mine is located in the Western Region at Tarkwa, as noted in the region's tourism overview. It is a major industrial site associated with Ghana's gold-mining heritage.

attractions.name: Bogoso Gold Mine
attractions.aliases: Bogoso Prestea Gold Mine; Bogoso Goldfields
attractions.description: Bogoso in the Prestea-Huni Valley Municipal District is a historic gold-mining town on the Ankobra River. Mining at Bogoso and neighbouring Prestea dates back to the colonial era and remains a major activity in the district.

attractions.name: Ankobra River
attractions.aliases: Ankobra; Ankobra River Ankobra
attractions.description: The Ankobra River is one of the largest rivers in the Western Region, rising in the highlands and flowing to the Gulf of Guinea near Axim. It was historically important for gold trade and passes through towns such as Bogoso and Bamianko.

attractions.name: Nkroful Ancestral Home
attractions.aliases: Nkroful; Kwame Nkrumah Birthplace; Nkroful Museum
attractions.description: Nkroful in the Ellembelle District is the birthplace of Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president, and is celebrated as a heritage site. The Nzema community is the site of his original family home and associated memorial structures.

attractions.name: Mount Afadja
attractions.aliases: Mount Afadjato; Afadjato; Mountain Afadja
attractions.description: Mount Afadja, known as Afadjato to the Ewe people, is one of the highest mountains in Ghana, with its summit in the Volta Region near the Togo border. It is one of the most visited tourist attractions in the Volta Region and lies in the Agumatsa Range.

attractions.name: Mount Adaklu
attractions.aliases: Adaklu Mountain; Mount Adaklu Summit
attractions.description: Mount Adaklu is a mountain about 12 km from Ho in the Adaklu District, standing roughly 580 m above sea level and venerated by nearby Ewe villages. Guided tours of the mountain are organised for tourists, with profits invested in the community.

attractions.name: Tafi Agome Caves
attractions.aliases: Tafi Agome Caves; Tafi Agome; Agome Caves
attractions.description: The Tafi Agome Caves are a cave site in the Volta Region listed among the region's tourist attractions alongside the Tafi Atome Monkey Sanctuary. They are associated with the historical refuge traditions of the Tafi communities.

attractions.name: Amedzofe Falls
attractions.aliases: Amedzofe Waterfall; Amedzofe Falls
attractions.description: Amedzofe Falls is a waterfall in the Volta Region listed among the region's waterfalls and tourist attractions. It is found in the mountainous Amedzofe area of the Ho West District.

attractions.name: Biakpa Falls and Caves
attractions.aliases: Biakpa Waterfalls; Biakpa Caves; Biakpa Falls
attractions.description: Biakpa Falls and Caves are a waterfall and cave attraction in the Volta Region listed among the region's waterfalls and tourist sites. They are located in the Avatime area near the Ghana-Togo borderlands.

attractions.name: Kpoeta Waterfalls
attractions.aliases: Kpoeta Falls; Kpoeta waterfalls Ho West
attractions.description: Kpoeta Waterfalls is a waterfall attraction in the Ho West District of the Volta Region, listed among the region's waterfalls. It lies in the forested hills of the district.

attractions.name: Akpom Falls and Logba Tota Cave
attractions.aliases: Akpom Falls; Logba Tota limestone cave; Logba Tota
attractions.description: Akpom Falls and the limestone cave at Logba Tota are natural attractions in the Volta Region listed among the region's waterfalls and caves. They are located in the Logba area of the Hohoe and Afadjato South districts.

attractions.name: Liate Wote Snake Village
attractions.aliases: Liate Wote Snake Village; Liati Wote Snake Farm
attractions.description: The Snake Village at Liate Wote is a wildlife attraction in the Volta Region listed among the region's tourist sites. It is located near Mount Afadja and Tagbo Falls in the Afadjato South District.

attractions.name: Adidime Waterfalls
attractions.aliases: Adidime Falls Klefe; Adidime Waterfalls
attractions.description: Adidime Waterfalls is a waterfall at Klefe in the Ho Municipal area of the Volta Region, listed among the region's tourist attractions. It lies in the hills close to Ho.

attractions.name: Ave Crocodile Resort
attractions.aliases: Ave Dakpa Crocodile Resort; Ave Crocodile Farm
attractions.description: The Ave Crocodile Resort is a wildlife and leisure attraction at Ave Dakpa in the Akatsi North District of the Volta Region. It is listed among the region's tourist attractions and features a crocodile pond.

attractions.name: Tordzie Falls
attractions.aliases: Tordzie Waterfalls; Tordzi Falls
attractions.description: Tordzie Falls is a waterfall on the Tordzie River near Kpandu in the Volta Region, popular with visitors for its cascades and surrounding vegetation. It is one of several waterfalls found in the region.

attractions.name: Kwafie Festival
attractions.aliases: Kwafie; Kwafie Festival Dormaa; Dormaa Kwafie
attractions.description: The Kwafie Festival is an annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Dormaa, Berekum and Nsoatre in the Bono Region in November, December or January. It commemorates the ancestors and purification, and features a large bonfire in the palace courtyard.

attractions.name: Munufie Festival
attractions.aliases: Munufie; Munufie Festival Drobo; Drobo Munufie
attractions.description: The Munufie Festival is celebrated by the people of Drobo in the Bono Region to cleanse and feed the stools and gods. It is climaxed with a large bonfire in the palace courtyard and re-enacts the legend that the people of Dormaa brought fire to Ghana.

attractions.name: Akwantukese Festival
attractions.aliases: Akwantukese; Akwantukese Festival Suma; Suma Akwantukese
attractions.description: The Akwantukese Festival is celebrated by the people of Suma in the Bono Region in March. It commemorates the historic migration of the Suma people and is observed with traditional rites and a durbar.

attractions.name: Akyiriwia Festival
attractions.aliases: Akyiriwia; Akyiriwia Festival Atomfourso; Atomfourso Akyiriwia
attractions.description: The Akyiriwia Festival is celebrated by the people of Atomfourso near Seikwa in the Tain District of the Bono Region. It is marked by a ban on noise making and funerals before the main celebration.

attractions.name: Sunyani Central Market
attractions.aliases: Sunyani Market; Sunyani Central Market
attractions.description: Sunyani Central Market is the principal trading market of Sunyani, the capital of the Bono Region, which is known as the green city of Ghana and a major conference destination. It serves as a hub for the region's agricultural produce and crafts.

attractions.name: University of Energy and Natural Resources
attractions.aliases: UENR; University of Energy and Natural Resources Sunyani
attractions.description: The University of Energy and Natural Resources is a public university in Sunyani, the capital of the Bono Region. It is one of the region's flagship public institutions and contributes to research on energy and natural resource management.

attractions.name: Sunyani Technical University
attractions.aliases: Sunyani Polytechnic; Sunyani Technical University
attractions.description: Sunyani Technical University, formerly Sunyani Polytechnic, is a public tertiary institution in Sunyani in the Bono Region. It is one of the region's principal educational landmarks.

attractions.name: Berekum Traditional Area
attractions.aliases: Berekum; Berekum Traditional Council; Berekum Township
attractions.description: Berekum is a major town in the Bono Region and the seat of the Berekum Traditional Area, whose chiefs join the Kwafie Festival celebrations. The town is a centre of cashew and timber production in the region.

attractions.name: Wenchi Traditional Area
attractions.aliases: Wenchi; Wenchi Traditional Council; Wenchi Township
attractions.description: Wenchi is a town in the Bono Region and the capital of the Wenchi Municipal District, with a long-established traditional chieftaincy. It lies near Bui National Park and the Bui Dam.

attractions.name: Dormaa Ahenkro Palace
attractions.aliases: Dormaa Palace; Dormaa Ahenkro Traditional Palace
attractions.description: Dormaa Ahenkro is the capital of the Dormaa Central Municipal District and the seat of the Dormaa Traditional Area. Its palace courtyard is the setting for the bonfire rituals of the Munufie and Kwafie festivals.

attractions.name: Banda Ahenkro Heritage Area
attractions.aliases: Banda Ahenkro; Banda Traditional Area; Banda
attractions.description: Banda Ahenkro is the capital of the Banda District in the Bono Region, at the foot of the Banda Mountains near Bui National Park. The area is associated with the historic Banda kingdom and its heritage sites.

attractions.name: Nsawkaw Township
attractions.aliases: Nsawkaw; Nsawkaw Tain; Nsawkaw Town
attractions.description: Nsawkaw is the capital of the Tain District in the Bono Region and one of the closest towns to Bui National Park. It is a growing commercial centre on the road to the Bui Dam.

attractions.name: Sampa Border Market
attractions.aliases: Sampa; Sampa Market; Sampa Border Town
attractions.description: Sampa is the capital of the Jaman North District in the Bono Region and a border town on the Ghana-Côte d'Ivoire frontier. Its market serves cross-border trade in agricultural produce and manufactured goods.

attractions.name: Japekrom Township
attractions.aliases: Japekrom; Jaman South; New Drobo
attractions.description: Japekrom is the capital of the Jaman South Municipal District in the Bono Region. It is a commercial and administrative centre serving the surrounding farming communities.

attractions.name: Odumase Township
attractions.aliases: Odumase; Odumase Sunyani West; Odumase Bono
attractions.description: Odumase is the capital of the Sunyani West District in the Bono Region, close to the regional capital Sunyani. It is an administrative and residential centre in the Sunyani conurbation.

attractions.name: Nkrankwanta Township
attractions.aliases: Nkrankwanta; Dormaa West; Nkrankwanta Town
attractions.description: Nkrankwanta is the capital of the Dormaa West District in the Bono Region. It lies in a productive cocoa and cashew growing area near the Côte d'Ivoire border.

attractions.name: Wamfie Township
attractions.aliases: Wamfie; Dormaa East; Wamfie Town
attractions.description: Wamfie is the capital of the Dormaa East District in the Bono Region. It is an agricultural and administrative centre in the eastern part of the Dormaa traditional area.

attractions.name: Jinijini Township
attractions.aliases: Jinijini; Berekum West; Jinijini Town
attractions.description: Jinijini is the capital of the Berekum West District in the Bono Region. It serves the surrounding cocoa, cashew and food-crop farming communities.

attractions.name: Buoyem Caves and Bat Colony
attractions.aliases: Buoyem Caves; Buoyem Bat Cave; Buoyem Caves and Bats Colony
attractions.description: The Buoyem Caves and bats colony lie within the locality of Buoyem in the Techiman Municipality of the Bono East Region. The dry semi-deciduous forest houses a large colony of rosetta fruit bats, caves, sandstone rocks and waterfalls.

attractions.name: Tanoboase Sacred Grove and Shrine
attractions.aliases: Tano Boase Sacred Grove; Tano Sacred Grove and Shrine; Tanoboase Sacred Grove
attractions.description: The Tanoboase Sacred Grove and Shrine is near the village of Tanoboase in the Techiman Municipality and is believed to be the cradle and traditional home of the Bono people. It became a Community Based Ecotourism Project in 1996 and is part of Ghana's material cultural heritage.

attractions.name: Tano River Sacred Fish
attractions.aliases: Tano Sacred Fish; Tanoso Sacred Fish; Tano River Sacred Fish Pond
attractions.description: The Tano River Sacred Fish site is located at Tanoso near Techiman in the Bono East Region. It houses a pool of sacred fish jealously protected by the community, said to have golden crowns.

attractions.name: Forikrom Boten Caves and Shrines
attractions.aliases: Forikrom Boten Caves; Boten Caves and Shrines; Forikrom Magic Cave
attractions.description: Forikrom Boten Caves and shrines are located about eight kilometres off the Techiman-Nkoranza road in the Bono East Region. The range of giant rocks forms a shrine and caves, and the largest cave is believed to have been a refuge for women and children in times of war.

attractions.name: Kristo Boase Monastery
attractions.aliases: Kristo Boase Monastery; Kristo Boase; Benedictine Monastery Bono East
attractions.description: Kristo Boase Monastery is home to a small community of eleven Benedictine monks in the Bono East Region. The monastery is set in a place of great beauty and historic interest and welcomes visitors from around the world each year.

attractions.name: Bono Manso Slave Trade Site
attractions.aliases: Bono Manso; Manso; Bono-Manso
attractions.description: Bono Manso, located on the Techiman-Kintampo road, was the capital of the Bono state from the 11th century to 1723 and a key node in the Trans-Saharan trade network. It is marketed today as a heritage site associated with the slave trade and is visited by members of the African diaspora.

attractions.name: Apoo Festival
attractions.aliases: Apoo; Apo Festival; Apoo Festival Bono East
attractions.description: The Apoo Festival is celebrated in the Bono East Region and is listed among the region's festive celebrations. It is a traditional festival during which grievances may be aired and social harmony is renewed.

attractions.name: Kurubi Festival
attractions.aliases: Kurubi; Kurubi Festival Kintampo; Wangara Kurubi
attractions.description: The Kurubi Festival is celebrated by the people of Kintampo in November, mainly to unite all Wangara descent in Ghana. Virgins normally dance on stilts as an interesting part of the festival.

attractions.name: Nkyifie Festival
attractions.aliases: Nkyifie; Nkyifie Festival Prang; Prang Nkyifie
attractions.description: The Nkyifie Festival is celebrated by the people of Prang in the Pru West District in September and October. It is listed among the festive celebrations of the Bono East Region.

attractions.name: Fokuo Festival
attractions.aliases: Fokuo; Fokuo Festival Nkoranza; Sessiman Ntoa
attractions.description: The Fokuo Festival is a notable festival celebrated by the people of Nkoranza (Sessiman) in the Bono East Region. It honours the deity called Ntoa, also known as Seesiman Ntoa, who played a critical role in leading the historical wars of the people of Nkoranza.

attractions.name: Techiman Central Market
attractions.aliases: Techiman Market; Techiman Central Market; Techiman Great Market
attractions.description: Techiman Central Market is one of the largest trading markets in Ghana and the commercial hub of the Bono East Region, whose capital is Techiman. It draws traders from across the region for yam, maize, beans, cassava and other produce.

attractions.name: Techiman Municipality
attractions.aliases: Techiman; Techiman Municipal District; Techiman City
attractions.description: Techiman is the capital of the Bono East Region and the seat of the Techiman Municipal District. It succeeded Bono Manso as the leading commercial centre of the area after 1723.

attractions.name: Kintampo Municipality
attractions.aliases: Kintampo; Kintampo North Municipal District; Kintampo Town
attractions.description: Kintampo is the capital of the Kintampo North Municipal District in the Bono East Region. It is a major town on the Kumasi-Tamale road and a base for visiting Kintampo Waterfalls and Fuller Falls.

attractions.name: Yeji Fishing Harbour
attractions.aliases: Yeji; Yeji Harbour; Yeji Fishing Port
attractions.description: Yeji is the capital of the Pru East District in the Bono East Region and a fishing town on the shores of Lake Volta. Fishing activities take place along the region's side of Lake Volta and Yeji is a centre of the trade.

attractions.name: Atebubu Market
attractions.aliases: Atebubu; Atebubu Market; Atebubu-Amantin
attractions.description: Atebubu is the capital of the Atebubu-Amantin Municipal District in the Bono East Region and a commercial centre for yam and food-crop trade. It is listed among the principal towns where yam production is high in the region.

attractions.name: Kwame Danso Township
attractions.aliases: Kwame Danso; Sene West; Kwame Danso Town
attractions.description: Kwame Danso is the capital of the Sene West District in the Bono East Region, one of the towns where yam production is high. It is an administrative and trading centre in the Sene area near Lake Volta.

attractions.name: Mim Bour
attractions.aliases: Mim Rocky Mountains; Mim Buo; Mim Bour Mountains
attractions.description: A group of three rocky peaks rising to about 410 m just west of Mim; the tallest is traditionally regarded as the father of the other two. The site has been partly developed for tourism with a reception centre, pool and gardens on the summit of the female mountain.

attractions.name: Mim Lake
attractions.aliases: Anwomasu Lake; Mim Anwomasu Lake
attractions.description: A small inland lake on the outskirts of Mim, expanded from the natural Anwomasu river, that is preserved as a tourist and leisure site. It holds endemic and near-endemic cichlid fish including Hemichromis frempongi.

attractions.name: Mim Airstrip
attractions.aliases: Mim Airfield; Mim Airport
attractions.description: An airstrip serving the Mim area, located east of the Mim Bour mountains. It is one of the few aviation facilities in the Ahafo Region.

attractions.name: Anwomasu Dam
attractions.aliases: Mim Dam; Anwomasu Reservoir
attractions.description: A dam near Ayum Forest Products in Mim, connected by a conduit to Mim Lake, that historically served industrial and domestic water purposes.

attractions.name: Okomfo Anokye Tree
attractions.aliases: Okomfo Anokye Historic Tree; Sankore Sacred Tree
attractions.description: A historic tree at Sankore associated with the legendary priest Okomfo Anokye and regarded as a sacred and heritage site in the Ahafo Region.

attractions.name: Tano River
attractions.aliases: Tano River; River Tano; Tanoe River
attractions.description: A 400 km river that drains the Tano Basin and flows through the forest belt around Goaso; it is culturally important to the Bono and Ahafo peoples and supports rich biodiversity.

attractions.name: Ahafo Mine
attractions.aliases: Newmont Ahafo Mine; Ahafo Gold Mine
attractions.description: One of the largest open-pit gold mines in Ghana, located in the Kenyasi area and operated since 2007, with estimated reserves of around 17 million ounces of gold.

attractions.name: Adekyem Festival
attractions.aliases: Adekyem Festival; Bechem Adekyem
attractions.description: An annual November festival celebrated by the people of Bechem that commemorates historical events from the town's founding and raises funds for local educational development.

attractions.name: Abetiase Festival
attractions.aliases: Abetiase Festival; Goaso Abetiase
attractions.description: A bi-annual festival held at Goaso that celebrates local traditions and the town's historic role in relation to the Golden Stool.

attractions.name: Addae Tuntum Festival
attractions.aliases: Akwasidae Tuntum Festival; Kukuom Addae Tuntum; Addae Tuntum
attractions.description: An annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Kukuom-Asunafo in the Ahafo Region, usually held in December or January. It commemorates the 18th-century Ebirimoro war between the Sefwi and Ahafo peoples and reaffirms the people's commitment to their chief.

attractions.name: Adikanfo Festival
attractions.aliases: Adikanfo Festival; Hwidiem Adikanfo; Adikanfo
attractions.description: An annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Hwidiem in the Ahafo Region, usually in September. It features a durbar of chiefs, drumming and animal sacrifices, and commemorates the migration of the people of Hwidiem from Denkyira Ntomu to their present home.

attractions.name: Apomasu Festival
attractions.aliases: Apomasu Yam Festival; Ntotroso Apomasu; Apomasu
attractions.description: An annual yam harvest festival held in January by the chiefs and people of Ntotroso-Asutifi in the Ahafo Region. It has been commemorated for more than 900 years and is used to pay homage to the Apomasu shrine.

attractions.name: Nkompo Festival
attractions.aliases: Nkompo Festival; Acherensua Nkompo; Nkompo
attractions.description: An annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Acherensua-Asutifi in the Ahafo Region, usually in January or September. It features a durbar of chiefs, traditional dress, dancing and drumming, and marks a historic event of the past.

attractions.name: Akwansramu Festival
attractions.aliases: Akwansramu Festival; Mim Akwansramu; Akwansramu
attractions.description: A December festival celebrated by the people of Mim in the Ahafo Region. Its name is a Twi term for espionage, and it commemorates the Asante warriors' patrol of the Mim-Akwaboa lands that averted an enemy incursion on Kumasi.

attractions.name: Ayum Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Ayum Forest Reserve; Ayum Reserve; Ayum Forest
attractions.description: A 112 km2 forest reserve established in 1940 in the Asunafo South District of the Ahafo Region. Connected to the Subim and Bonsam Bepo reserves, it protects Guinean moist forest biodiversity including chimpanzees, elephants and other endangered species.

attractions.name: Bonsam Bepo Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Bonsam Bepo Forest Reserve; Bonsam Bepo Reserve; Bosam Bepo
attractions.description: A 124 km2 forest reserve established in 1934 at Ahantamo near Akrodie in the Ahafo Region. It forms part of a 488 km2 forest complex together with the Ayum and Subim reserves.

attractions.name: Kasapin Tuesday Market
attractions.aliases: Kasapin Market; Kasapin Tuesday-weekly market; Kasapin Weekly Market
attractions.description: A vibrant weekly market held every Tuesday in Kasapin, Asunafo North, in the Ahafo Region. It draws traders and buyers from Accra, Kumasi, Mim, Goaso and Kwadwo Addaikrom.

attractions.name: Cathedral of St. Anthony
attractions.aliases: Cathedral of St. Anthony; Goaso Cathedral; St. Anthony Cathedral Goaso
attractions.description: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Goaso, located in Goaso, the capital of the Ahafo Region. The diocese was established in 1997 from the Diocese of Sunyani.

attractions.name: Danso Abaim Festival
attractions.aliases: Danso Abaim Festival; Techimantia Danso Abaim; Danso Abaim
attractions.description: A traditional festival celebrated at Techimantia in the Tano South area of the Ahafo Region, listed among the festivals of the former Brong Ahafo area. Techimantia is one of the major towns of the Ahafo Region.

attractions.name: Mim Cashew Plantation
attractions.aliases: Mim Cashew; Mim Cashew Plantation; Mim Cashew & Agric Products
attractions.description: Cashew plantations in the Mim area of the Ahafo Region that supply the Mim Cashew and Agricultural Products Ltd factory, producer of the Mim Cashew Brandy.

attractions.name: Gbewaa Palace
attractions.aliases: Naa Gbewaa Palace; Yaa Naa Palace; Gbewaa palace
attractions.description: The royal palace at Yendi, traditional capital of the Kingdom of Dagbon, and the seat of the Yaa Naa, king of Ghana's oldest kingdom.

attractions.name: Deutsch Cemetery
attractions.aliases: German Cemetery Yendi; Deutsch Cemetery at Yendi
attractions.description: A colonial-era cemetery at Yendi associated with the period of German involvement in the region, listed among the Northern Region's heritage sites.

attractions.name: Tamale Center for Culture and Arts
attractions.aliases: Tamale Cultural Centre; Tamale Centre for Culture and Arts
attractions.description: A cultural centre in Tamale showcasing the arts, crafts and traditions of the peoples of the Northern Region.

attractions.name: Nkrumah Volini
attractions.aliases: Nkrumah Volini; Nkrumah Historic Site
attractions.description: A historic site in Tamale associated with Kwame Nkrumah and the nationalist movement in northern Ghana.

attractions.name: Nuku Studio
attractions.aliases: Nuku Studios; Nuku Art Studio
attractions.description: An art studio in Tamale contributing to the city's contemporary visual arts scene.

attractions.name: Diarre Napagaduungbanani
attractions.aliases: Diarre Napagaduungbanani; Diare Heritage Site
attractions.description: A traditional heritage site at Diare in the Northern Region recognised for its historical and cultural significance.

attractions.name: Sabali River (River Oti)
attractions.aliases: Sabali; River Oti at Sabali; Sabali River
attractions.description: A stretch of the River Oti at Sabali in the Northern Region, noted as a scenic riverine site.

attractions.name: Nawuni River (White Volta)
attractions.aliases: Nawuni River; White Volta at Nawuni
attractions.description: The White Volta River at Nawuni, an important waterway and scenic natural site in the Northern Region.

attractions.name: Tamale Central Mosque
attractions.aliases: Tamale Central Mosque; Tamale Mosque
attractions.description: The principal central mosque of Tamale, one of the city's best-known landmarks and a focal point of Islamic worship in northern Ghana.

attractions.name: Tamale Central Market
attractions.aliases: Aboabo Market; Tamale Central Market
attractions.description: The main market of Tamale, a major trading hub for grains, livestock, yams and crafts from across the Northern Region.

attractions.name: Aliu Mahama Sports Stadium
attractions.aliases: Tamale Sports Stadium; Aliu Mahama Stadium
attractions.description: Tamale's principal stadium, formerly the Tamale Sports Stadium, which hosted matches during the 2008 African Cup of Nations.

attractions.name: Tamale International Airport
attractions.aliases: Tamale Airport; Tamale International Airport
attractions.description: The airport serving Tamale, located about 11 km from the city centre and operating regular domestic flights to Accra and other regional capitals.

attractions.name: Tamale Teaching Hospital
attractions.aliases: Tamale Teaching Hospital; TTH
attractions.description: Ghana's third-largest hospital and the main referral health facility for the Northern Region, also used for medical teaching and research.

attractions.name: Dakpema Palace
attractions.aliases: Dakpema Palace; Dakpema Chief's Palace
attractions.description: The palace of the Dakpema, the traditional chief of Tamale, whose influence shaped the city's establishment as an administrative centre.

attractions.name: Larabanga Mystic Stone
attractions.aliases: Larabanga Mystery Stone; Mystic Stone of Larabanga
attractions.description: A sacred stone on the outskirts of Larabanga believed to return to its original position whenever it is moved; British road builders reportedly had to divert a road around it in the 1950s.

attractions.name: Larabanga Baobab (Ayuba's Grave)
attractions.aliases: Larabanga Baobab; Ayuba's Baobab; Baobab of Larabanga
attractions.description: A baobab beside the Larabanga Mosque that is reputed to mark the grave of Ayuba, the mosque's founder, and whose leaves are used locally for healing.

attractions.name: Bole Mosque
attractions.aliases: Bole Mosque; Old Bole Mosque
attractions.description: A Sudano-Sahelian adobe mosque in the centre of Bole, dated to around the 17th century, which collapsed in 2023 and was rebuilt with traditional materials in 2024.

attractions.name: Bui Reservoir
attractions.aliases: Bui Lake; Bui Reservoir
attractions.description: The reservoir created by the Bui Dam, with a surface area of up to 440 km2 and a haven for hippos, cormorants and other wildlife.

attractions.name: Bui Gorge
attractions.aliases: Bui Gorge; Bui Gap
attractions.description: The rocky gorge on the Black Volta where the Bui Dam is built, noted for its dramatic terrain and first surveyed by geologist Albert Ernest Kitson in 1925.

attractions.name: Salaga Slave Market
attractions.aliases: Salaga Slave Market; Salaga Old Slave Market
attractions.description: The site of the largest slave market in 18th- and 19th-century Ghana, from which captives were shipped to the coast; a young baobab now marks the former market area.

attractions.name: Salaga Slave Tree
attractions.aliases: Salaga Slave Tree; Slave Tree of Salaga
attractions.description: A historic tree at Salaga associated with the town's role in the trans-Saharan and Atlantic slave trades and preserved as a heritage landmark.

attractions.name: Wonkan Bawa (Slave Bathing Pond)
attractions.aliases: Wonkan Bawa; Slave Bathing Spot
attractions.description: A pond at Salaga whose Hausa name means the bathing spot of slaves, recalling the town's history as a major slave market.

attractions.name: Jakpa Palace
attractions.aliases: Ndewura Jakpa Palace; Yagbonwura Palace
attractions.description: The seat, official residence and meeting place of the Yagbonwura, overlord of the Gonja Kingdom, located at Damongo and built in Malian architectural style.

attractions.name: St Anne's Catholic Cathedral
attractions.aliases: St Anne's Cathedral Damongo; Saint Anne's Catholic Cathedral
attractions.description: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Damongo and one of the town's principal landmarks.

attractions.name: Gonja Kingdom Traditional Seat
attractions.aliases: Yagbonwura Seat; Gonja Kingdom Seat
attractions.description: Damongo has been the seat of the Gonja Kingdom since the Yagbonwura's court moved there from Nyange in 1944, making it a centre of Gonja heritage.

attractions.name: Kpembe Traditional Area
attractions.aliases: Kpembe; Kpembewura Traditional Area
attractions.description: A traditional town just 2 km from Salaga that serves as the capital of the Kpembe Traditional Area, whose chief is the overlord of Salaga.

attractions.name: Mole Safari Lodge
attractions.aliases: Mole Motel; Mole Safari Lodge
attractions.description: The accommodation and visitor complex at Mole National Park, described as West Africa's first luxury safari lodge and the base for park game drives and walking safaris.

attractions.name: Salaga Slave Wells
attractions.aliases: Salaga Slave Wells; Salaga Wells
attractions.description: Historic wells at Salaga that supplied water to the town's slave market and caravans, listed among the Savannah Region's tourism sites.

attractions.name: NaJeringa Defence Wall
attractions.aliases: NaJeringa Wall; NaJeringa Defence Wall
attractions.description: A historic wall built in the 1700s by a Mamprusi king to defend the capital at Nalerigu against raiders; its remains are preserved as a heritage site.

attractions.name: Zayaa Mosque-Shrine
attractions.aliases: Zayaa Mosque; Zayaa Shrine; Zayaa Mosque/Shrine
attractions.description: A distinctive mosque and shrine at Wulugu with an intriguing mystical and spiritual history, noted for its unusual architecture.

attractions.name: Ancient Koma Figurines
attractions.aliases: Koma Figurines; Koma Terracotta Figurines
attractions.description: Clay statuettes left behind by settlers over 1,000 years ago, discovered in the Yikpabongo area and important to West African archaeology.

attractions.name: Tusugu Cliff Dwellings
attractions.aliases: Tusugu Cliff Dwellings; Tusugu Cliff Settlement
attractions.description: Well-preserved remains of an ancient settlement built into the Gambaga Escarpment, discovered in 1961.

attractions.name: Gingana Mountain & Rock Art
attractions.aliases: Gingana Mountain; Gingana Rock Paintings
attractions.description: A scenic point on the Gambaga Escarpment overlooking the White Volta, notable for its ancient rock carvings and paintings.

attractions.name: Kpatiritinga Rock Art & Granaries
attractions.aliases: Kpatiritinga Rock Art; Kpatiritinga Granaries
attractions.description: A site along the Gambaga Escarpment with rock art and centuries-old adobe granaries, among the region's most impressive recent archaeological discoveries.

attractions.name: Tanfiok-Naamaa Rock Paintings
attractions.aliases: Tanfiok-Naamaa Rock Paintings; Jilik Rock Paintings
attractions.description: Prehistoric rock paintings of hunters and animals near Jilik that researchers believe may date back to the Stone Age.

attractions.name: White Volta River Rapids
attractions.aliases: White Volta Rapids; White Volta River Rapids
attractions.description: A stretch just north of Gambaga where the White Volta rushes through rocks, creating dramatic rapids along the base of the escarpment.

attractions.name: Gbintiri Market
attractions.aliases: Gbintiri Market; Gbintri Market
attractions.description: Held every six days, this is the largest market in the North East Region, drawing traders and livestock from across the area.

attractions.name: The Doves' Caves (Nmana Feeri)
attractions.aliases: Doves' Caves; Nmana Feeri; Doves Caves Nalerigu
attractions.description: A group of rock outcrops a short hike from Nalerigu, popular for bouldering, exploring and views over the surrounding savanna.

attractions.name: Fire Festival (Bugum Chugu)
attractions.aliases: Bugum Chugu; Fire Festival; Bugum Festival
attractions.description: An exciting annual festival celebrated in most Mamprusi communities across the region in remembrance of an old legend, marked by night-time fire processions.

attractions.name: Damba Festival
attractions.aliases: Damba Festival; Damba; Damma Festival
attractions.description: A major annual festival of the Mamprusi and Dagomba peoples, celebrated at the NaYiri Palace in Nalerigu with drumming, dancing and traditional regalia.

attractions.name: Birimi Prehistoric Site
attractions.aliases: Birimi Site; Birimi Prehistoric Site
attractions.description: An archaeological site near Nalerigu associated with the Kintampo Complex civilisation and ancient pearl millet cultivation.

attractions.name: Mamprusi and Mossi Kings' Gravesites
attractions.aliases: Gambaga Gravesites; Mossi Chiefs' Gravesites
attractions.description: Ancestral grave sites of ancient Mamprusi and Mossi kings at Gambaga, which was once the residence of Mamprusi kings.

attractions.name: Gambaga Witch Camp
attractions.aliases: Gambaga Witch Camp; Gambaga Witches Camp
attractions.description: A settlement at Gambaga where women accused of witchcraft have historically sought refuge; it featured in the 2011 documentary The Witches of Gambaga.

attractions.name: Red Volta River
attractions.aliases: Red Volta; Red Volta River
attractions.description: One of the two Volta headstreams flowing through the North East Region, offering canoeing and riverside scenery alongside the White Volta.

attractions.name: Nakpanduri Escarpment
attractions.aliases: Nakpanduri Escarpment; Nakpanduri Scarp
attractions.description: A dramatic section of the Gambaga Escarpment at Nakpanduri, known for its cliffs, caves and panoramic views across the North East Region.

attractions.name: White Volta River
attractions.aliases: White Volta; White Volta River
attractions.description: The major river of the North East Region, which together with the Red Volta forms the Volta River and is popular for canoeing.

attractions.name: Whispering Rocks and Shrines of Tongo
attractions.aliases: Whistling Rocks of Tongo; Tongo Whispering Rocks; Tengzug Whistling Rocks
attractions.description: A rock formation in Tengzug where one rock rests on another and emits strange whistling sounds in November and December. It is a notable natural landmark of the Tongo Hills.

attractions.name: Tono Dam
attractions.aliases: Tono Irrigation Dam; Navrongo-Tono Irrigation Dam; Tono Reservoir
attractions.description: One of the largest agricultural dams in West Africa, a 2 km dam in the Kassena-Nankana District that irrigates about 2,490 hectares. Construction began in 1975 and was completed in 1985.

attractions.name: Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of Seven Sorrows
attractions.aliases: Navrongo Cathedral; Navrongo Mud Church; Our Lady of Seven Sorrows Basilica
attractions.description: A Roman Catholic cathedral and minor basilica in Navrongo and one of the oldest churches in Ghana. Its historic mud-built structure is a well-known regional monument.

attractions.name: Wuriyanga Mosque
attractions.aliases: Wuriyanga Ancient Mosque; Wuriyanga Mud Mosque
attractions.description: A historic Sudano-Sahelian style mosque in the Upper East Region located southeast of Bawku and beyond Garu. It is a regional heritage site.

attractions.name: Pwalugu Hydroelectric Power Station
attractions.aliases: Pwalugu Dam; Pwalugu Hydro-Solar Hybrid Plant; Pwalugu Power Station
attractions.description: A 60 MW hydroelectric power station under construction on the White Volta at Pwalugu. It is planned to combine with a solar plant to form Ghana's first hydro-solar hybrid power project.

attractions.name: Navrongo Solar Power Station
attractions.aliases: Navrongo Solar Plant; Navrongo Solar Farm
attractions.description: A 2.5 MW solar power plant in Navrongo, Upper East Region. It is one of Ghana's early utility-scale solar generation facilities.

attractions.name: Sirigu Art and Pottery Village
attractions.aliases: SWOPA; Sirigu Pottery and Arts Centre; Sirigu Women's Organisation for Pottery and Art
attractions.description: A community art and pottery centre in Sirigu known for hand-painted pottery, basketry and decorated architecture. The SWOPA centre hosted UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan in 2002.

attractions.name: Bolgatanga Market
attractions.aliases: Bolga Market; Bolgatanga Central Market; Bolga Basket Market
attractions.description: A major twice-weekly market in Bolgatanga where farmers and traders sell livestock and the region's famous woven baskets, leather goods and straw handicrafts.

attractions.name: Bolgatanga Craft Village
attractions.aliases: Bolga Craft Village; Bolgatanga Arts and Crafts Village
attractions.description: A craft centre in Bolgatanga showcasing the region's basket weaving, leatherwork and metal jewellery. It sits adjacent to the Upper East Regional Museum.

attractions.name: Bongo Rocks
attractions.aliases: Bongo Rock Formations; Bongo Hills; Bongo Rocks Landscape
attractions.description: Distinctive granite rock outcrops around Bongo in the Upper East Region. They form part of the region's savannah landscape near the Burkina Faso border.

attractions.name: Kukula Mystery Dam
attractions.aliases: Kukula Dam; The Mystery Dam of Kayoro
attractions.description: A small sacred dam at Kayoro in the Kassena-Nankana area traditionally regarded as mysterious. It lies near Paga and the Burkina Faso border.

attractions.name: Nasaga Game Reserve
attractions.aliases: Nasaga Game Reserve; Nasaga Wildlife Reserve
attractions.description: A game reserve about 8 km from Paga and the Burkina Faso border. It protects savannah wildlife in the far north-east of the Upper East Region.

attractions.name: Gologo Festival
attractions.aliases: Gologo/Golib Festival; Golib Festival; Gologo Festival of the Talensi
attractions.description: An annual festival celebrated by the Talensi of Tongo-Zug in March before the planting of grain. Sacrifices are offered for rain and a good harvest, followed by public dancing.

attractions.name: Fao Festival
attractions.aliases: Fao Harvest Festival; Fao Festival of Paga; Fao Thanksgiving Festival
attractions.description: A harvest thanksgiving festival held at Paga, Chiana and Kayoro between November and February. Farmers display stalks of their first millet harvest in gratitude to the gods.

attractions.name: Samanpiid Festival
attractions.aliases: Samanpiid Festival of the Kusasi; Samanpiid Harvest Festival
attractions.description: An annual harvest festival celebrated by the Kusasi people of the Bawku Traditional Area in November and December. It gives thanks to the gods for a good harvest.

attractions.name: Boaram Festival
attractions.aliases: Boaram Festival of the Gurunsi; Boaram Harvest Festival
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the Gurunsi (Frafra) people of the Upper East Region. It is associated with harvest thanksgiving and traditional music and dance.

attractions.name: Tengana Festival
attractions.aliases: Tengana Festival; Tengana Festival of Balungu; Tengana Festival of Winkongo
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the people of Balungu, Winkongo and Pwalugu in the Upper East Region. It honours the earth deity and the ancestors.

attractions.name: Ndaakoya Festival
attractions.aliases: Ndaakoya Festival; Ndaakoya Festival of the Frafra
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the Frafra, Talensi and Nabdam-speaking communities of the Upper East Region. It is a cultural gathering featuring music and dance.

attractions.name: Gwollu Defence Wall
attractions.aliases: Gwollu Slave Defence Wall; Gwollu Slave Trade Defence Wall; Gbollu Defence Wall
attractions.description: A 19th-century wall built by Gwollu Koro Limann as a defence against slave raiders. It is one of Ghana's best-preserved relics of the slave trade era.

attractions.name: Gbele Resource Centre
attractions.aliases: Gbele Game Production Reserve; Gbelle Game Reserve; Gbele Resource Reserve
attractions.description: One of Ghana's largest game reserves, located about 17 km south of Tumu. It protects roan antelope, hippos, elephants and many bird species and is the fourth largest reserve in Ghana.

attractions.name: Nakore Mosque
attractions.aliases: Nakore Ancient Mosque; Nakore Mud Mosque
attractions.description: A small historic mosque in Nakore, southwest of Wa, built in the Sudano-Sahelian architectural style. It is one of the region's ancient Sudanese mosques.

attractions.name: Dondoli Mosque
attractions.aliases: Dondoli Ancient Mosque; Dondoli Mud Mosque
attractions.description: A 19th-century mosque in the village of Dondoli in Wa, built in the Sudano-Sahelian style. It is now in partial ruins and is a protected heritage site.

attractions.name: Wechiau Mosque
attractions.aliases: Wechiau Ancient Mosque; Wechiau Mud Mosque
attractions.description: A historic mosque in the village of Wechiau in the Upper West Region. It is one of the region's traditional Sudano-Sahelian mosques.

attractions.name: Hippo Hide Tree House
attractions.aliases: Hippo Hide; Hippo Hide Treehouse; Wechiau Tree House
attractions.description: A tree-house lodge in the Wechiau Community Hippo Sanctuary overlooking the Black Volta. It allows visitors to watch hippos and birds from an elevated hide.

attractions.name: Bulenga Caves
attractions.aliases: Bulenga Ancient Caves; Bulenga Slave Caves
attractions.description: Ancient caves at Bulenga that served as refuges during the slave raids in the Upper West Region. They are among the region's historic cave sites.

attractions.name: Dahili Caves
attractions.aliases: Dahili Ancient Caves; Dahili Slave Caves
attractions.description: Historic caves at Dahili used as hiding places during the 19th-century slave raids. They form part of the Upper West Region's slave-trade heritage.

attractions.name: Sankana Caves
attractions.aliases: Sankana Ancient Caves; Sankana Slave Caves
attractions.description: Caves at Sankana that provided refuge from slave raiders in the pre-colonial period. The site is associated with local resistance to slave raids.

attractions.name: Kassana Slave Camp
attractions.aliases: Kassana Slave Market; Kassana Slave Camp and Market
attractions.description: A former slave camp and market site in the Upper West Region linked to the trans-Saharan and Atlantic slave trade routes.

attractions.name: Tomb of Hilla Limann
attractions.aliases: Hilla Limann Tomb; Dr. Hilla Limann Grave
attractions.description: The tomb of Dr. Hilla Limann, a former president of Ghana, who was born and raised in Gwollu. It is one of the town's principal heritage attractions.

attractions.name: Kaleo Solar Power Station
attractions.aliases: Kaleo Solar Plant; Kaleo Power Station
attractions.description: A 13 MW solar power plant at Kaleo developed by the Volta River Authority between 2020 and 2022. Its output is fed into Ghana's national grid.

attractions.name: Black Volta River
attractions.aliases: Mouhoun River; Volta Noire; Black Volta
attractions.description: A major river that forms Ghana's north-western border with Burkina Faso along the Upper West Region. It supports the Wechiau hippo sanctuary and is a key regional waterway.

attractions.name: George Ekem Ferguson's Tomb
attractions.aliases: George Ferguson Tomb; Ferguson's Tomb
attractions.description: The preserved tomb of George Ekem Ferguson, a Ghanaian colonial agent killed by slave raiders in 1897. It is located in Wa and is maintained as a historic site.

attractions.name: Wa Airport
attractions.aliases: Wa Regional Airport; Wa Airstrip
attractions.description: An airport serving Wa and the Upper West Region. It connects the regional capital by air and supports travel to the north-west of Ghana.

attractions.name: Dumba Festival
attractions.aliases: Dumba Festival of the Wala; Dumba Festival
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the Wala people of Wa that includes a ritual testing the chief's fitness to rule. It is marked by drumming, dancing and a durbar.

attractions.name: Kobine Festival
attractions.aliases: Kobine Festival of Lawra; Kobina Festival
attractions.description: A post-harvest festival celebrated by the people of Lawra in early October. It acknowledges the spiritual guidance of the ancestral gods and features dancing competitions.

attractions.name: Kakube Festival
attractions.aliases: Kakube Festival of Nandom; Kakube Festival
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the Nandom people in late November to early December. It thanks the family gods and asks them to bless the soil and protect the people.

attractions.name: Paaragbiele Festival
attractions.aliases: Paragbiele Festival; Paaragbiele Festival of Tumu
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the Tumu people to thank the ancestors and God for guidance over the farming season. Farm produce is exhibited alongside music and dance.

attractions.name: Tinmaale Festival
attractions.aliases: Tinmaale Festival of Hain; Tinmaale Festival
attractions.description: A festival celebrated by the residents of Hain in the Jirapa District of the Upper West Region.

attractions.name: Mount Dzebobo
attractions.aliases: Mount Dzebobo; Dzebobo Mountain; Mont Dzebobo
attractions.description: Ghana's second highest mountain at 876 metres, on the Togo border just south of Kyabobo National Park. Its name means 'seen from afar' in the Ewe language.

attractions.name: Hanging Village, Shiare
attractions.aliases: Shiare Hanging Village; The Hanging Village; Shiare Mountain Settlement
attractions.description: A nine-century-old village settlement built in the Breast Mountains of the Oti Region. It is known as 'The Hanging Village' because of its steep mountain setting.

attractions.name: Kete Krachi Ferry Crossing
attractions.aliases: Kete Krachi Ferry; Krachi Ferry; Volta Lake Ferry
attractions.description: A ferry service linking Kete Krachi to Kwadjokrom across Lake Volta. It is an important transport link for the Oti Region.

attractions.name: Akwantutenten Festival
attractions.aliases: Akwantutenten Festival; Akwantutenten Festival of Worawora
attractions.description: An annual festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Worawora in the Jasikan District in September. It is observed by the Akan communities of the area.

attractions.name: Rice Festival
attractions.aliases: Rice Festival of Akpafu; Akpafu Rice Festival
attractions.description: An annual harvest festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Akpafu in the Oti Region. It is held in January and celebrates the local rice harvest.

attractions.name: Kete Krachi Festival
attractions.aliases: Kete Krachi Festival; Krachi Festival
attractions.description: A festival celebrated in the Kete Krachi area of the Oti Region. It is one of the region's principal cultural events.

attractions.name: Nanaba Festival
attractions.aliases: Nanaba Festival; Nanaba Festival of the Oti Region
attractions.description: A festival celebrated in the Oti Region and listed by the Ghana Tourism Authority among its key cultural events.

attractions.name: Kyabobo Waterfalls
attractions.aliases: Kyabobo Falls; Kyabobo Lower Fall; Kyabobo Waterfalls
attractions.description: Waterfalls inside Kyabobo National Park in the Oti Region. They are among the park's visitor attractions.

attractions.name: Kyabobo Hiking Trails
attractions.aliases: Kyabobo Trails; Kyabobo Hiking and Mountain Biking Trails
attractions.description: Seven hiking trails and two mountain-biking trails in Kyabobo National Park. The most popular trail follows a ridge to a peak on one of the Breast Mountains.

attractions.name: Bia National Park
attractions.aliases: Bia National Park; Bia National Park and Resource Reserve
attractions.description: A 563 sq km national park in the Bia West District, established as a park in 1974 and part of a UNESCO biosphere reserve. It protects some of Ghana's last untouched forest, with 62 mammal species and over 189 bird species.

attractions.name: Bia Resource Reserve
attractions.aliases: Bia Resource Reserve; Bia Reserve
attractions.description: The southern part of the Bia Conservancy Area in the Western North Region. Together with Bia National Park it forms a twin conservation area and biosphere reserve.

attractions.name: Bia Conservancy Area
attractions.aliases: Bia Biosphere Reserve; Bia Conservancy Area; Bia UNESCO Biosphere Reserve
attractions.description: A designated UNESCO biosphere reserve in the Western North Region covering nearly 306 sq km. It contains the Bia National Park and the Bia Resource Reserve.

attractions.name: Chirano Gold Mine
attractions.aliases: Chirano Gold Mine; Asante Gold Chirano; Chirano Mine
attractions.description: An underground and open-pit gold mine in the Western North Region within the Bibiani gold belt. It is operated as Asante Gold Chirano Ltd.

attractions.name: Awaso Bauxite Mine
attractions.aliases: Ghana Bauxite Company Mine; Awaso Bauxite Mine
attractions.description: A bauxite mine at Awaso near Bibiani operated by the Ghana Bauxite Company. It is served by a branch of the western Ghana rail system.

attractions.name: Bia River
attractions.aliases: Bia River; River Bia
attractions.description: A transboundary river that drains the Bia conservation zone in the Western North Region, including Sefwi, Aowin and Suaman. It empties into Aby Lagoon on the Ghana-Ivory Coast border.

attractions.name: Dadieso Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Dadieso Forest Reserve; Dadieso Reserve
attractions.description: A forest reserve located at Dadieso, the capital of Suaman District in the Western North Region.

attractions.name: Apaso Sacred Site
attractions.aliases: Apaso; Apaso Sacred Site; Apaso Cultural Site
attractions.description: A sacred cultural site inside Bia National Park near two small pools. Visitors traditionally sacrifice and give gifts to the gods there.

attractions.name: Alluolue Festival
attractions.aliases: Alluolue Festival; Eluo Festival; Sefwi Yam Festival
attractions.description: An annual yam festival celebrated by the chiefs and people of Sefwi Wiawso and Sefwi Bekwai, usually in July. It is the common yam festival of the Sefwi traditional states.

attractions.name: Boin Tano Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Boin Tano Forest Reserve; Boin Tano Reserve; Boin-Tano
attractions.description: A 129 km2 nature reserve established in 1968 in the Western North Region of Ghana. It is rich in both floral and faunal species.

attractions.name: Krokosua Hills Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Krokosua Hills Forest Reserve; Krokosua Hills; Krokosua Reserve
attractions.description: A 481 km2 forest reserve established in 1935 in the Western North Region of Ghana. It is noted for chimpanzee reports and as habitat of the critically endangered Krokosua squeaking frog.

attractions.name: Cathedral of St. Joseph
attractions.aliases: Cathedral of St. Joseph; Wiawso Cathedral; St. Joseph Cathedral Wiawso
attractions.description: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Wiawso, located at Wiawso in the Western North Region. The diocese was established in 1999 from the Diocese of Sekondi-Takoradi.

attractions.name: Bibiani Gold Project
attractions.aliases: Bibiani Gold Project; Bibiani Gold Mine; Bibiani Mine
attractions.description: An underground gold mine development at Bibiani in the Western North Region, being developed by Asante Gold. The town of Bibiani is the capital of the Bibiani/Anhwiaso/Bekwai Municipal Assembly.

attractions.name: Disue River
attractions.aliases: Disue River; Desue River; River Disue
attractions.description: A tributary of the Tano River, also called the Desue, that flows through the township of Enchi, capital of the Aowin Municipality in the Western North Region.

attractions.name: Tano Nimri Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve; Tano-Nimire Forest Reserve; Tano Nimri FR
attractions.description: A 206 km2 forest reserve established in 1935 in south-western Ghana, lying in the Enchi Forest District and sharing a boundary with the Boin Tano reserve. It is designated an Important Bird Area and is thought to hold western chimpanzees.

attractions.name: Tano Anwia Forest Reserve
attractions.aliases: Tano Anwia IBA; Tano-Anwia Forest Reserve
attractions.description: A forest reserve near Enchi in the Aowin Municipality of Ghana's Western North Region. It is recognised by BirdLife International as an Important Bird Area.

attractions.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral, Wiawso
attractions.aliases: Cathedral of St. Joseph; St Joseph Cathedral Wiawso; Wiawso Catholic Cathedral
attractions.description: The Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Wiawso, listed among the cathedrals of Ghana, in the regional capital Sefwi Wiawso.

attractions.name: Cathedral Church of the Ascension, Sefwi Wiawso
attractions.aliases: Cathedral Church of Ascension; Ascension Anglican Cathedral Sefwi-Wiawso
attractions.description: An Anglican cathedral of the Church of the Province of West Africa, listed at Sefwi-Wiawso in Ghana's Western North Region.
